source.label: thm:convergence
source.quote: Suppose that the players of a monotone game follow (MD-b) with step-size gamma_n and query radius delta_n such that lim gamma_n = lim delta_n = 0, sum gamma_n = infinity, sum gamma_n delta_n < infinity, and sum gamma_n^2/delta_n^2 < infinity. Then, the sequence of realized actions hat X_n converges to Nash equilibrium with probability 1.

results.notes: This is an asymptotic convergence statement with no rate, recorded as limsup of the distance to the Nash-equilibrium set = 0 almost surely.

source.label: thm:rate
source.quote: Let x* be the (necessarily unique) Nash equilibrium of a beta-strongly monotone game. If the players follow (MD-b) with Euclidean projections and parameters gamma_n = gamma/n and delta_n = delta/n^{1/3} with gamma > 1/(3 beta) and delta>0, we have E[||hat X_n - x*||^2] = O(n^{-1/3}).

results.notes: The bound is on the squared distance of the realized actions to the Nash equilibrium at round n (here T = n). Theorem 9(b) in the appendix restates the same result. Tuning the step size requires knowing the strong-monotonicity constant beta_sm, which is not the canonical smoothness beta.

conditions: oracle unbiased with finite conditional second moment V^2

source.label: thm:rates
source.quote: If the players have access to a gradient oracle satisfying (oracle) and they follow (MD) with Euclidean projections and step-size sequence gamma_n = gamma/n for some gamma > 1/beta, we have E[||X_n - x*||^2] = O(n^{-1}).

results.notes: This is part (a) of Theorem 9. Part (b) duplicates Theorem 2.
